title: In the Drops: Clever Redshift pedal adapters, SunGod high-contrast glasses, handy Stubble & Co backpack and Cameron Winter

In the Drops: Clever Redshift pedal adapters, SunGod high-contrast glasses, handy Stubble & Co backpack and Cameron Winter

It’s the Blackest of Fridays and this year I am thankful for you, for reading this article focused around probably full price products (spoiler: there are deals here too) when half the internet is 30% off. You are the real MVPs.

If you are interested in deals, be sure to check out our Black Friday roundup though, which has been lovingly put together by the industry’s most prolific talent Paul Norman.

Elsewhere on the website this week, Paul has also updated our gravel bike tyres guide, and we’ve finished up our road bike mudguard reviews with this lovely buyer’s guide from Mildred Locke.

The latest episode of the Cyclist Magazine Podcast is available now too, featuring author Gareth Cartman talking about the 1926 Tour de France, the toughest of them all.

And finally, tech editor Sam Challis unleashed his latest Tech Talk newsletter onto cyclist.co.uk, and he thinks he’s found the one bike to do it all.

Let’s get in the drops, don’t forget your gloves it’s cold out.

Redshift Mousetrap pedal adapters

Sometimes you see a product and it’s an immediate ‘yes’, that was our reaction when Redshift revealed the Mousetrap SPD pedal adapters. We’ve finally got our hands on them a few months later, and yes keeps yessing.

These clever contraptions attach onto clipless pedals to make them grippy flat pedals – very handy if you use the same bike at the weekend and on your commute, for those who want system flexibility or for journalists who find themselves unexpectedly bringing a new bike home from work without the right shoes to hand.

They’re made from glass-reinforced nylon, attach and detach easily while staying secure when in use, and when not in use they’re lightweight and small enough to fit in a pocket and are conveniently magnetised to keep them together.

They can be used either two per pedal for a full flat setup or one per pedal for a hybrid system, and because they attach to the clipless pedal they should keep you at the right saddle height unless you’ve got platforms on.

After initially launching with the SPD model, Redshift has now launched SPD-SL and Look Keo versions. I’m particularly looking forward to getting a set on power meter pedals to prove how overrated clipless is.

  • Buy now from Redshift Sports (£37.49 – currently 25% off)

SunGod Vulcans Vent glasses with Plum lens

Tis the season for parking your sunglasses in their nice cloth bag and dusting off the clear and photochromic lenses. For the 2026 darkness, SunGod has launched two new lenses for low and changing light conditions: the 8KO Iris Gold photochromic lens and this, the 8KO Plum high-contrast fixed-tint lens.

Not only does it look fantastic, but the Plum lens helps to enhance contrast, making obstacles and hazards more visible in dull and dark conditions. They have a Fixed Category 2 Tint, meaning they let 31% of light through, and SunGod says they maintain the 100% UV protection needed to fully protect your eyes.

So far I’ve been using them on my commute, where their protection from the elements has been vital for my eyes and their high-contrast has helped me spot the immeasurable number of hazards riding through London.

  • Buy now from SunGod (£150)

Stubble & Co Hybrid backpack

I used to be happy with any old cheap backpack – surely spending money on a bag doesn’t make it that much better than the old reliable Amazon Basics? I was young and naive, I can only apologise. Great bags are great bags, and especially if you’re the kind of person to accumulate all sorts in a backpack that just gets lost in a disorganised system, a well thought-through design is one of the most underrated things you can invest in.

Stubble & Co’s Hybrid backpack is exactly that. It’s been designed to meet working, training and day-to-day needs with a split zone system that will make even the most disorganised among us feel like Marie Kondo.

Going back to front, features include: a padded sleeve for attaching to luggage; an Air-Flow back panel for breathability; adjustable chest straps; rear opening with padded laptop sleeve; main compartment – in this case 20 litres, which has a suitcase-like clamshell opening to make everything easy access; a smaller zip pocket inside the main compartment; compressions straps; an elasticated bottle pocket; a hidden front pocket; and TPU-coated water-resistant zips.

On top of that, it’s made with ergonomics in mind, with padded straps and all sorts of adjustability. It also has extra loops to attach extras such as lights or carabiners, has a handle both on top and on the side, and is made with durable waterproof materials and weather-proof bound seams.

Have that Bezos.

  • Buy now from Stubble & Co (£108 – currently 30% off)

What we’re into this week: Cameron Winter, ‘Live at Carnegie Hall’

I will keep breaking cups until my left hand looks wrong. Until my miracle drugs write the miracle song. I will keep rolling down until my best shirt rolls of. Until the conga line behind me is a thousand chickens long.

Imagine opening one of the great albums of the last few years with that and shortly after becoming one of the youngest artists ever to play a headline show at Carnegie Hall, which just so happens to be filmed by Oscar winner Paul Thomas Anderson.

It seems like every winter is a Cameron winter at this point, and in 2026 that means the release of his Live at Carnegie Hall album and the film of that show.

I loved the Heavy Metal studio album, and Winter’s live versions take the whole thing to another level. It is absolutely sublime and weird and very good. Highly recommend.
